issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts (ticking exhaust leak)
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the engine bay that is loudest on a cold start, sometimes an exhaust smell inside or around the truck, and in some cases a check engine light.
issues.why: The bolts holding the cast-iron exhaust manifolds to the 6.0L cylinder heads snap after years of heating and cooling. Once a bolt breaks, exhaust leaks past the gasket. Owners have reported this on many H2s, sometimes with damage to nearby parts.
issues.next: Have the manifold area checked for broken bolts. A leak near the cabin can let exhaust fumes in, so do not ignore a strong exhaust smell. Broken bolts usually have to be drilled out, so pick a shop that has done this job before.

issues.t: Speedometer and gauges stick or stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer, tachometer or other gauges freeze, jump around, drop to zero at speed or stop working entirely. Warning lights may come on together or the cluster backlighting may fail.
issues.why: Components inside the instrument cluster fail with age, especially the small motors that move the needles. Owners report it at many mileages on these years.
issues.next: Use a phone GPS app to check your speed until it is fixed. A cluster rebuild service is an option besides a new dealer cluster, which also needs programming.

issues.t: Wipers turn on by themselves or stop working
issues.sym: The windshield wipers run on their own, will not shut off, work only now and then, or stop in the rain. The washer pump may also keep spraying until the reservoir is empty.
issues.why: Water gets into the wiper motor and its control module at the base of the windshield, which corrupts the module. GM recalled some 2003 trucks for this, but owners of other years report the same thing.
issues.next: Do not drive in rain or snow with wipers that may quit. Pulling the wiper fuse stops a runaway wiper temporarily. Ask a dealer whether your VIN is covered by a recall, then replace the wiper motor/module if not.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers that work only sometimes or stop working, reducing your view in bad weather.
issues.why: On some 2003 H2s, water could enter the wiper motor module, and an earlier campaign covered wiper motors that were built incorrectly. GM recalled the affected trucks.
issues.next: Have a Hummer/GM dealer run your VIN for open recalls. The fix (a module cover or new motor) is free.

issues.t: Air blows from the wrong vents or will not cool
issues.sym: Air only comes out of the defrost vents, the A/C blows warm air, or you cannot change where the air comes out. You may hear a clicking behind the dash.
issues.why: An electric mode or blend door actuator behind the dashboard fails. It is the small motor that moves the flaps that send air to each vent or mix hot and cold.
issues.next: Have the HVAC system scanned to find which actuator has failed. It is usually a modest repair, and a battery change or disconnect can trigger a relearn.

issues.t: Blower motor wiring or resistor overheats
issues.sym: A burning electrical smell, the fan working only on some speeds or cutting out, and in some reports melted plastic or smoke near the glove box.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor and its wiring connector carry a lot of current and can overheat. Owners report melted connectors and harnesses on many H2 model years.
issues.next: Turn the fan off and get it checked if you smell burning plastic. The resistor and its connector or pigtail should be replaced together.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines burst (pedal sinks to the floor)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly goes soft or sinks to the floor, brake fluid leaks under the truck, or the brake warning light comes on.
issues.why: The steel brake lines that run under the truck rust, especially where roads are salted, and eventually burst. Owners report sudden loss of braking with little warning.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft, stop driving and have the truck towed. On older H2s, have the brake lines inspected for heavy rust and replace them before they fail.

issues.t: Hydro-boost brake accumulator can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A heavier brake pedal and harder steering, or power steering fluid leaking near the brake booster.
issues.why: The H2 uses the power steering pump to power its brakes (hydro-boost). The pressure reservoir on certain Bosch units can crack and come apart, letting fluid out and reducing brake and steering assist. GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the brakes or steering suddenly feel heavy, stop safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Hydro-boost relief valve seal may fracture (recall)
issues.sym: Slightly heavier steering when braking or parking, and a brake pedal that needs a little more push to stop the truck.
issues.why: Some hydro-boost brake housings were machined out of spec, which can break the O-ring seal on the relief valve. The trucks did not meet the federal brake standard, so GM recalled them.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN. The free repair is a new relief valve.

issues.t: Heated washer fluid system fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Washer fluid heater problems, an electrical burning smell, smoke from under the hood, or other electrical faults.
issues.why: The heated windshield washer system had a circuit board and ground wire that could short and overheat. GM issued recalls, first adding a fused harness and later disabling the module, because it could start a fire.
issues.next: Make sure the heated washer recalls are done on your VIN. Until then, stop using the heated washer feature and have it checked if you smell burning.

issues.t: Front ball joint or steering knuckle failure
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, wandering steering, uneven tire wear, and in the worst cases a front wheel that collapses or comes off the truck.
issues.why: The heavy H2 and its big tires put high loads on the front ball joints and steering knuckles. Owners report ball joints snapping and front wheels separating, sometimes at speed.
issues.next: Have the ball joints and knuckles checked at every tire rotation, especially on lifted trucks or those with larger tires. Replace worn joints right away.

issues.t: Loose, wandering steering (worn pitman and idler arms)
issues.sym: Steering feels vague or loose at highway speed, the truck wanders in its lane, or the steering wheel has play.
issues.why: The pitman arm and idler arm that connect the steering box to the front wheels wear out under the H2’s weight. Owners often add a heavy-duty reinforcement kit when replacing them.
issues.next: Have the steering linkage inspected and the front end aligned after any repair. Worn steering parts can also make braking feel unsettled.

issues.t: Power steering leaks and hard steering
issues.sym: Steering gets hard to turn, especially when parking, power steering fluid drips under the truck, or the pump whines.
issues.why: Leaks at the power steering pump, cooler or hoses let fluid run low. Because the brakes share this fluid (hydro-boost), a leak can also affect braking. GM also recalled some power steering hoses built out of spec.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. Fix leaks quickly, since low fluid can damage the pump and affect brake assist. Ask a dealer about open hose recalls.

issues.t: No-start from theft system or ignition switch
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start or will not crank at all, sometimes with a security light, then starts after waiting several minutes. The key may stick in the ignition.
issues.why: The Passlock theft-deterrent system and the ignition switch or lock cylinder can fail with wear, so the computer stops fuel or cranking.
issues.next: Note whether the security light is on when it will not start. A shop can read the theft-system codes; the fix is usually an ignition switch, lock cylinder or Passlock sensor.

issues.t: Airbag light on (airbag module or water damage)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and stays on, sometimes with a service message or other modules acting up.
issues.why: The airbag control module (SDM) can fail, and some owners trace it to rain water leaking into the cabin near the module.
issues.next: The airbags may not work while the light is on. Have the codes read, fix any water leak first, then repair or replace the module.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Water drips onto the front floor or seats, the headliner gets wet, or the carpet smells musty after rain.
issues.why: The drain tubes at the corners of the sunroof tray clog with debris, so rain water overflows into the cabin instead of draining out.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and tested. Dry the carpet promptly to prevent mold and damage to wiring under the floor.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or stuck in gear
issues.sym: Slipping between 1st and 2nd, flaring engine revs, delayed engagement, or the transmission sticking in one gear.
issues.why: The heavy-duty 4-speed automatic behind the 6.0L works hard moving a 6,400-pound truck, and its clutches wear out. Owners report slipping and stuck-in-gear problems.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and smell. Have it diagnosed before it gets worse; frequent towing or big tires make wear faster.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic shifts harshly or loses drive
issues.sym: Harsh or erratic shifts, a transmission warning code, or the truck suddenly losing power to the wheels when pulling away.
issues.why: The 6-speed automatic used with the 6.2L engine can develop internal faults; owners report early failures and transmission codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked as soon as shifts change. A software update or valve body repair sometimes helps; a failed unit needs a rebuild.

issues.t: Front differential seal and transmission cooler line leaks
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the truck or a small leak at the front differential or transmission cooler lines.
issues.why: Seals on the front differential and fittings on the transmission cooler lines can seep, even on low-mile trucks.
issues.next: Have the leak located and fixed before fluid levels drop, which can damage the differential or transmission.

issues.t: Power window falls into door or stops working
issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, makes a grinding noise, or drops down into the door.
issues.why: The window regulator cable or motor in the door fails. Owners report rear windows dropping and getting stuck open.
issues.next: Tape plastic over the opening to keep rain out until it is fixed. The regulator and motor are often replaced together.

issues.t: Paint peeling on rear quarter panels
issues.sym: Paint flakes or peels from the rear quarter panels.
issues.why: Owners of these H2s report paint adhesion failing on the rear quarters.
issues.next: Repaint the area before the panel starts to corrode under the bare spots.

issues.t: Front doors freeze shut after rain
issues.sym: Front doors are hard to open or frozen shut in winter after rain or washing.
issues.why: Water collects in the front door jambs and seals and freezes.
issues.next: Dry the door jambs after washing in cold weather and treat the seals with a silicone protectant.

issues.t: Heated seats turn on by themselves or overheat
issues.sym: A seat heater comes on by itself, will not turn off, or gets very hot; one owner found damaged wiring in the seat cushion.
issues.why: The heated seat element or its control switch and module can fail.
issues.next: Unplug or fuse off the seat heater until it is fixed if it overheats. Have the heater element and control switch checked.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hub failure
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed, play in the wheel, or an ABS warning light.
issues.why: The sealed front wheel bearing and hub assemblies wear out on this heavy truck. One owner had a dealer find bad front bearings after a driving problem.
issues.next: Have the noise checked; a failing bearing can overheat and let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: ABS and traction control lights come on
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights flicker on and off; in one case gauges, windows and locks lost power at the same time.
issues.why: Faults in the ABS control module or wheel speed sensor wiring set warning lights. GM also recalled some trucks for reversed wheel speed sensor wires.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal braking still works, but ABS and traction control may be off.

issues.t: Frame and subframe rust
issues.sym: Clicking when turning the steering wheel, heavy rust on the frame and underbody, or rusted-through brackets.
issues.why: Road salt corrodes the H2’s frame and steel underbody parts. A dealer traced one owner’s clicking to a rusted subframe support.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected, especially on trucks from snowy states. Treat rust early with an undercoating; severe rust needs welding repair.

issues.t: Fuel pump flow control module failure
issues.sym: Hard starting, stalling or loss of power, with fuel system codes.
issues.why: The module that controls fuel pump speed on these trucks can fail. One owner was told their VIN was not included in a related recall.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether any recall or warranty extension covers your VIN, then have the fuel pump control module tested.

issues.t: Low oil pressure or failing lifters
issues.sym: Low oil pressure warning, a ticking or tapping from the engine, or the gauge reading lower than normal.
issues.why: Owners report collapsed or failed valve lifters and low oil pressure on high-mileage 6.0L engines.
issues.next: Stop driving if the oil pressure light comes on. Check the oil level, then have a shop test oil pressure before more damage occurs.

issues.t: Radiator leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant spots under the front of the truck, a low coolant warning, or the temperature gauge reading high.
issues.why: The radiator can develop leaks; one 6.2L owner had theirs replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Top up with the right coolant and watch the gauge. Replace a leaking radiator before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor wiring breaks down
issues.sym: The engine stalls or will not start, sometimes only now and then.
issues.why: The wiring pigtail for the crankshaft position sensor becomes brittle from engine heat and shorts out.
issues.next: Have the crank sensor and its wiring checked. Repairing the wiring and replacing the sensor is usually a modest job.

issues.t: Stumbles and stalls right after a cold start
issues.sym: The engine coughs, stutters or stalls right after starting, sometimes with harsh shifting.
issues.why: An owner reported this happening daily on a nearly new 6.2L truck and the dealer found no fix. The cause was not identified.
issues.next: Have the engine and transmission codes read and ask about software updates. Keep notes of when it happens to help the shop.
